notes:
RULING ON THE APPROVAL-WORKFLOW QUESTION (the curator's flagged uncertainty). The contract admits them, and the corpus supports it. QUESTIONS.md §3 inclusion criterion 1 is 'a specific, identifiable requester — a human or a system acting for one (DocuSign envelope; the expense-approval workflow ... where Maya is the designated approver)', and the matching exclusion is narrow: 'automated reminders with no human requester behind them (a SaaS "your trial expires" is nobody waiting)'. The test is therefore whether a named human has already done their half and is stuck at the owner's step. Applying it: JE-2291 passes on its face — 'was submitted by Miles Okonkwo and is pending your approval' (c40f18c2e4b60028) — it fails only on closure (see finding 2). VB-33107 passes — 'was approved by Karen Voss and routed to you for final sign-off' (c40f18c2e4b60029) — it fails only on double counting (finding 3). Ruth's Ramp limit passes — 'Ruth Amankwah has requested a monthly limit increase on her Ramp card' (c40f18c2e4b60033) — borderline is the right tier, since Ruth has never chased it. The Bill.com batch (c40f18c2e4b60030) is the weakest of the four on requester identity, since Bill.com names no individual sender, but it passes on the same principle: fourteen named vendors with due dates now past, and the body names the humans behind two of the lines ('the first installment of the FY26 audit fee and is due on receipt per the engagement letter Karen countersigned last week'), while 'Bill.com will release ACH payments automatically 24 hours after approval' establishes that nothing moves until Aditi clicks. Include it, at must_include. The line the set should hold consistently: a machine message with a named human behind the ask counts; a machine message with no human behind it does not — which is why the Gusto payroll approval (c40f18c2e4b60038, 'approve by Thursday, Aug 13 at 5:00pm ET', $418,910.40) and the Carta 409A sign-off (c40f18c2e4b60042) are correctly out of Q3 despite being loud and imminent. Both, plus the completed DocuSign envelope (c40f18c2e4b60045 answered by c40f18c2e4b60046) and PO-10482, deserve must_not_include entries — a naive system will return all four.

PO-10482 (c40f18c2e4b60027, $38,120, 'Requested by: Ruth Amankwah', 'Your approval is the final step before the purchase orders are released to each vendor') looks at first like a missed item of exactly the class above. It is not, and the reason is worth recording: its line items reappear as invoices in the Aug 7 payment batch — Precision Servo $14,300, Boston Bearing $6,930, Suffolk Steel $9,840+$2,220=$12,060, Cortland Cable $3,650 — which means the PO was released and the vendors have shipped and billed. Correctly omitted; add it as a distractor so the reasoning is visible.

finance-q3-01 (rank 1) survives, but not cleanly, and a human reviewer should see the argument on the other side. Nadia enumerated what was still outstanding twice after her Jul 24 escalation — c50f18c2e4b60005 (Aug 3): 'we're still missing four items off the PBC list: the lease amortization schedule, the related-party disclosures, the Q4 bank confirmations, and the fixed asset roll-forward', and c10f18c2e4b60044 (Aug 7): 'Two items ahead of fieldwork: the ASC 842 lease schedule for the Waltham warehouse, and a fresh Carta cap table export' — and the Meridian lease amendment appears in neither. That is the strongest closure-shaped evidence in the thread. It does not carry, for two reasons: no message anywhere shows the redline delivered, and Nadia's lists are demonstrably not exhaustive — she lists the Q4 bank confirmations as missing on Aug 3 although Aditi's own PBC tracker (attachment to c50f18c2e4b60024) marks them 'delivered' on Jul 25. Per the spec, silence and inconsistent re-listing do not close an obligation. Keep the item; the merge of nhaddad@pembertonwells.com and nadia.haddad.cpa@gmail.com into one requester is handled correctly.

Other candidates swept and correctly excluded: Karen's deferred-revenue reclass nudge (c60f18c2e4b60012, 'can you nudge him if you talk to him before I do?') died with the July close lock; the inventory-obsolescence memo Nadia wants (c20f18c2e4b60009) is explicitly assigned elsewhere — 'If Miles can turn that around by early next week' — and is addressed to four people; the ASC 606 memo (c20f18c2e4b60040, 'Send the memo over for the file when it's ready') is likewise group-addressed and owned by Miles; Derek's entertainment-cap thread (c50f18c2e4b60011) ends with Aditi's own answer and her own new promise ('I'll get you a one-page pre-approval exception process by Friday'), which is Q2, not Q3; the CFO Alliance panel logistics (c30f18c2e4b60024) are due Oct 1. All six existing distractors check out.
